title: A Byzantine Bath at Qalandia
author: D. C. Baramki
location_note: Qalandia, twelve kilometres north of Jerusalem; no map reference; placed by name. p. 105 from the contents; first leaf unnumbered.
notes: Found by villagers in Aug. 1931, then excavated: two room groups with mosaic and slab floors, furnace remains, plastered recesses ('stoups'), stepped tanks, basins, runnels and pipes; the excavator interprets the whole as a bathing establishment (caldarium, tepidarium, frigidarium) with a fire and rebuilding. Stepped tanks are coded as ritual_bath under plan section 5 (stepped pool, whatever the excavator's label); the excavator's label is 'tank' in a 'bath'. Iliffe (QDAP IV p. 80) later compared the Y.M.C.A. 'bath' to 'its analogue at Qalandia' as a cistern; that view is not applied here.

features.site: chambers C and E, and east of Group II
features.subtype: stepped plastered tanks (excavator: 'tank'): original tank with steps at both ends, later tank (a) with steps in the SW corner; tank (b) with four steps and sump; circular pit with two steps fed by a channel
features.period: Byzantine (title; ribbed sherds set in the plaster)
features.quote: Access to it was by a flight of steps

features.subtype: basin beside tank (a), roughly circular in its latest phase; tank (c) with sump and niche
features.quote: Tank (c) was paved and plastered in the same way

features.site: chambers B, C and east of Group II
features.subtype: runnel under the connecting door, pottery pipes into the original tank, funnel inlets, narrow channel to the stepped pit
features.quote: Two pottery pipes discharged into it from the north
